solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fellow to give others the chop

definitions.text: Fellow to give others the chop

parts.words: Fellow to give others the chop
parts.note: an executioner who beheads people with an axe, not a woodcutter or a manager making redundancies

explanation.surface: A man whose job is cutting other people down, perhaps a ruthless boss sacking staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The chop' sounds like being fired, but here it is literal: the axe on the block.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical executioner who cut off heads with an axe was called by this title.

clue.text: That's funny feature of many a country estate

definitions.meaning: the sound of laughter written out, said when something amuses

definitions.text: feature of many a country estate
definitions.meaning: a sunken ditch with a wall, keeping livestock out of a park without spoiling the view

explanation.surface: Someone laughing at the odd sight of a quirky landscape feature on a grand estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is written as two syllables of mirth, and the hidden sunken fence of English parkland carries the same name.

clue.text: A duke requires a bit of armour, one counsels

parts.note: a visor is the movable face guard of a helmet

explanation.surface: A nobleman needs a piece of armour, and someone gives him advice about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A counsellor is someone who gives guidance, the job of this kind of consultant.

clue.text: Chinese prophet of doom given a hearing

indicators.note: a word allowed to be heard, i.e. spoken, points to a sound-alike

parts.note: a cynic is a pessimist who always expects the worst

explanation.surface: A Chinese doom-monger is finally allowed to speak and be listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an adjective formed from the Latin name for China, used for things of Chinese origin.

clue.text: See a wise pundit learn about game — and learn less than half usually

parts.note: a sage is a wise person consulted for opinions

indicators.note: about signals the letters of learn being shuffled around

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the usual crossword game

indicators.note: taking fewer than half the letters of the second learn, just its opening pair

explanation.surface: An expert advises a student to study a sport, then learn only a fraction of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LEARN into NERAL; 'less than half' leaves LE, the first two of its five letters. 'See' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means normally or in most cases, an idiom for what happens typically.

clue.text: Dubious operation captured by this camera

indicators.note: the answer is caught within the words this camera, as a photo is caught by a lens

explanation.surface: A shady deal is caught on film by a security camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraudulent scheme or swindle is a questionable piece of business.

clue.text: German city once possibly holding a record

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
possibly says once could be rearranged into another order

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A German city that may once have held a record of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like 'formerly' but is fodder: 'possibly' rearranges it to CONE, and 'holding' splits that around the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Köln on the Rhine is known in English by this name, a major city in western Germany.

clue.text: More half-cut holiday-makers, not socially acceptable as road-users

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of More is kept
U means upper-class or socially acceptable, so this phrase says remove a U

parts.note: tourists are people on holiday

explanation.surface: More drunken holidaymakers behaving badly on the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' (British slang for tipsy) leaves MO; 'not socially acceptable' drops U, the old British label for upper-class usage, from TOURISTS to leave TORISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers of cars are among those who use the roads.

clue.text: It's not formal, in a manner of speaking

definitions.meaning: describes a relaxed, chatty style rather than an official one
read literally: in the manner of spoken talk

explanation.surface: A disclaimer that something is only loosely or figuratively true.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatty register is informal, and it is the style of everyday talk between people.

clue.text: WC stars as a quintessential Englishman

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, a WC
Taurus, the constellation, is the Bull

explanation.surface: A toilet with celebrities posing as a typical Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' is the constellation Taurus, whose name means bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon personification of England, a stout beef-eating farmer, bears this name.

clue.text: Nasty old woman drinking French wine in the past could be trying

indicators.note: drinking means the first piece takes in the second

parts.note: a hag is an ugly or spiteful old woman
vin is French for wine
ago means back in time

explanation.surface: A spiteful old woman drank French wine in the past, which might be trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' looks like an adjective (annoying) but means attempting.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an attempt at something is expressed by this informal idiom for having a try.

clue.text: Little bird, duck, getting damp across lake

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

indicators.note: across means the first piece stretches over the second

parts.note: wet means moist or damp
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A small bird and a duck get wet crossing a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a zero, so O, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a small bird, named with the diminutive ending meaning little.

clue.text: Note added by unknown revolutionary shows soul

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
Y is an algebraic unknown
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A note appended by a mysterious rebel reveals his inner self.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for the spirit or inner self is used in English for the mind or soul.

clue.text: Half a dozen close by imbibing good or bad wine?

parts.note: six, VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: near means nearby

explanation.surface: Six people nearby drinking wine that may be good or bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine that has soured turns into this acidic condiment; the name comes from French for sour wine.

clue.text: See how torturers cruelly dominated

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters are tortured and twisted out of order

explanation.surface: Observe how torturers ruled over their victims with cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person, traditionally a wife, who is the one in charge of a household.

clue.text: Now she's able to move, without the restrictions of stays made from this?

definitions.text: Now she's able to move, without the restrictions of stays made from this?

indicators.note: to move means the letters are shifted into a new order
the restrictions are the bounding letters, the first and last of stays

explanation.surface: A woman freed from her corset can finally move, the stays having been made of this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S and S, the ends of STAYS, from the pool before 'to move' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Corset stays were traditionally stiffened with baleen, the horny plates from a whale's mouth.

clue.text: Cardinal you found sitting on beach?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: thou is an old word for you
sand is what a beach is made of

explanation.surface: A churchman finds you sitting on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers, and this one is ten hundred.

clue.text: Oaf a lass soundly walloped — we wholeheartedly approve too!

indicators.note: walloped means battered, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A girl soundly beat a lout, and everyone cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cheer of agreement sung after the toast song for a good fellow, meaning everyone concurs.

clue.text: Person failing has gone off showing indignation

parts.note: a dud is a failure, someone who doesn't work out

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: A failure of a person has stormed off in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to be in a state of resentful anger.

clue.text: Number admitting pain hospital discharged in secret

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective meaning done secretly

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other piece in

parts.note: five is a number

indicators.note: discharged means sent out, as a patient leaves

parts.note: hurt means pain
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A number of patients admitted in pain are discharged from hospital on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' sends H out of HURT, leaving URT, which FIVE takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done stealthily, out of sight, is sly and secretive in manner.

clue.text: The last person something is intended for?

definitions.text: The last person something is intended for?

parts.words: The last person something is intended for?
parts.note: sounds like someone least deserving, but means the final consumer in a supply chain

explanation.definitionFit: The final consumer of a product or system, the one it is ultimately designed for.

clue.text: Natural cheat about to enter pub

indicators.note: to enter means going inside the other piece

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: about means turned round, so rob is read backwards

parts.note: to rob is to cheat someone out of something

explanation.surface: A born swindler is about to walk into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROB into BOR, which goes into INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality one is born with, innate rather than learned, is natural to one.

clue.text: No brother or sister should be brought up to be a brute

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: sib is short for sibling

explanation.surface: An only child raised without siblings is bound to turn out a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads NO SIB upward, giving BISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute can mean any large beast, and the American buffalo is one.

clue.text: Bottom group of pupils collecting top grade

indicators.note: collecting means gathering the other piece inside

parts.note: a set is a class of pupils grouped by ability
A is the highest grade

explanation.surface: The bottom set of pupils somehow collects a top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like the opposite of 'top grade', but it is the definition: the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: One's backside, the part one sits on, is a common informal sense.

clue.text: Article written on old church? It's pretty wet!

indicators.note: in an across clue, written on means placed after the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item written about an old church, with the punchline that it is rather damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast body of salt water is about as wet as anything can be, a playful description.

clue.text: I'd end all rambling around sea's edge?

definitions.text: I'd end all rambling around sea's edge?

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the other piece
rambling means wandering, so the letters stray out of order
the edge of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A walker vows to stop strolling along the coast, perhaps because the cliffs collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' turns I'D END ALL into LANDLIDE, which wraps S, the first letter of 'sea's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse of earth, as on an eroding coastline, would certainly end any cliff walk.

clue.text: Long periods of snooze on Sunday

indicators.note: of signals the answer is made from part of the words snooze on Sunday

explanation.surface: Long stretches of sleeping in on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages, aeons, immeasurably long spans of time, especially in geology.

clue.text: Mournful-sounding spy gathering information

indicators.note: gathering means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A melancholy-voiced spy collecting intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a loud, resonant, plaintive tone, like a tolling bell.
